subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: According to Genesis 1, on which day did God create human beings?
explanation: Genesis 1:24-31 says God made land animals and then humankind on the sixth day, after which he declared everything very good.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: In the second creation account, God made Eve from which part of Adam?
explanation: Genesis 2:21-22 says God took one of Adam's ribs while he slept and made it into a woman.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: What was the sign of God's covenant with Noah after the flood?
explanation: In Genesis 9:12-17 God set the rainbow in the clouds as a sign that he would never again destroy the earth by flood.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: What was the outward sign of God's covenant with Abraham and his descendants?
explanation: Genesis 17:10-11 commands that every male be circumcised as the sign of the covenant between God and Abraham's descendants.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: What did God do on the seventh day of creation?
options: Rested, blessed the day and made it holy
Gave Adam the animals to name
explanation: Genesis 2:2-3 says God finished his work, rested on the seventh day, blessed it and made it holy.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: Who succeeded Moses as leader of the Israelites and led them into Canaan?
explanation: Joshua son of Nun was commissioned by Moses and led Israel across the Jordan into Canaan.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: On which mountain did God give Moses the Ten Commandments?
explanation: The Ten Commandments were given to Moses on Mount Sinai (also called Horeb), as the covenant law for Israel.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: Which judge, with 300 men, defeated the Midianites using trumpets, empty jars and torches?
explanation: Judges 7 records that Gideon defeated the Midianites with 300 men carrying trumpets and torches inside jars.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: Why did the elders of Israel ask Samuel to give them a king?
options: Samuel's sons took bribes, and they wanted to be like other nations
Samuel had retired to Ramah as a priest
explanation: 1 Samuel 8 says Samuel's sons perverted justice, and the people wanted a king like the surrounding nations.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: Which promise did God make to David in the covenant of 2 Samuel 7?
options: That David would build the Temple himself
That his house and throne would be established forever
That Israel would never face war
That Jerusalem would never be captured
explanation: Through Nathan, God promised that David's house, kingdom and throne would endure forever; David's son, not David, would build the Temple.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: Why did Cain kill his brother Abel?
options: Cain was jealous that God accepted Abel's offering but not his
Abel refused to share his flock
explanation: Genesis 4:3-8 says God looked with favour on Abel's offering but not Cain's, and Cain's anger led him to murder Abel.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: Under Joshua, how did the walls of Jericho fall?
options: An earthquake struck on the first day
The people marched round the city for seven days and shouted when the trumpets sounded
Rahab opened the gates to the army
explanation: Joshua 6 says they marched round once a day for six days and seven times on the seventh, then shouted and the walls fell.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: On Mount Carmel, Elijah challenged the prophets of which god?
explanation: 1 Kings 18 records Elijah's contest with the 450 prophets of Baal, in which the LORD answered by fire.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: When God offered to give him whatever he asked, what did Solomon request?
options: An understanding mind to govern and discern right from wrong
explanation: 1 Kings 3:9 says Solomon asked for an understanding mind to judge the people, and God also gave him riches and honour.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: Why did God reject Saul as king in the matter of the Amalekites?
options: He spared King Agag and the best livestock against God's command
He refused to go to war
He worshipped the gods of the Philistines
He killed the priests at Nob
explanation: In 1 Samuel 15, Saul disobeyed the command to destroy Amalek completely, so Samuel announced that God had rejected him as king.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: Which tree in the Garden of Eden did God forbid Adam and Eve to eat from?
options: The tree of the knowledge of good and evil
The tree of wisdom and strength
explanation: Genesis 2:16-17 forbids eating from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, on pain of death.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: In Genesis 15, how did God ratify his covenant with Abram?
options: By commanding him to be circumcised
By a smoking fire pot and flaming torch passing between the divided animals
By writing laws on stone tablets
explanation: Genesis 15:9-17 describes a smoking pot and flaming torch, symbols of God's presence, passing between the halves of the sacrificed animals.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: Who were the two sons of Eli the priest whose wickedness led to the downfall of his house?
explanation: Hophni and Phinehas misused the sacrifices at Shiloh and were killed in battle, and Eli failed to restrain them (1 Samuel 2-4).

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: Why was Moses barred from entering the Promised Land?
options: He struck the rock at Meribah instead of speaking to it as God commanded
He broke the first tablets of stone
explanation: At Meribah (Numbers 20) Moses struck the rock in anger rather than obeying God's command to speak to it, so he did not enter Canaan.

subject: CRS
topic: Creation, covenant and leadership in the Old Testament
body: Which king began a religious reform after the Book of the Law was found in the Temple?
explanation: In 2 Kings 22-23, King Josiah renewed the covenant and removed idols after Hilkiah found the Book of the Law.
